prattle.definition: to talk in a foolish or excited way, often about unimportant things
examples: Stop prattling and help me with the homework.
They prattled about trivial topics.

parsimonious.definition: very unwilling to spend money, often in a way that seems too careful
examples: He was parsimonious with tips.
The parsimonious budget limited their options.

portage.definition: the act of carrying a boat and gear over land between two water areas
examples: They planned a short portage around the waterfall.
A portage is needed when the river becomes too shallow.

peal.definition: a loud ringing sound, especially of bells
examples: A peal of laughter filled the room.
We heard a peal of bells at noon.

plaint.definition: a formal statement of someone’s complaint, especially in court
examples: The plaint described the injuries in detail.
The court received the plaint.

poise.definition: a calm, controlled way of standing or speaking, often showing confidence
examples: She spoke with poise during the interview.
The athlete kept her poise even under pressure.

poise.definition: to balance or keep something steady in position; also to consider or judge carefully
examples: Poise the glass carefully on the tray.
She poised her decision after reviewing the facts.

piebald.definition: having black and white patches, often describing animals such as dogs or horses
examples: The piebald dog had one black ear.
A piebald pattern covered the horse’s coat.

pinch.definition: to squeeze something slightly between fingers; also to take a small amount from a supply
examples: Pinch the fabric to see if it is loose.
I’ll pinch a bit of sugar from the jar.

pinch.definition: a small painful squeeze or a small amount of something
examples: Be careful, the pinch is small but it hurts.
Add a pinch of salt.

pith.definition: the most important part or main meaning of something
examples: Tell me the pith of the argument.
The pith of the story is simple.

penurious.definition: very unwilling to spend money; extremely cheap
examples: He is penurious with even small expenses.
The penurious landlord refused to fix the plumbing.

proscenium.definition: the front opening of a theatre stage, framed by the stage wall
examples: The actors waited behind the proscenium before entering.
The lights changed as the performance crossed the proscenium.

pit.definition: a deep hollow in the ground
examples: They found an old pit near the fence.
The ground collapsed into a pit.

pit.definition: the area of seats in a theatre directly in front of the stage, used by an orchestra
examples: The conductor stood up in the pit.
The sound from the pit filled the hall.

pit.definition: a sports or entertainment area where an audience or activities are close to the action
examples: The event was held in a fenced pit.
Crowds gathered in the pit for the final match.

peeve.definition: a small thing that annoys someone repeatedly
examples: Clean hands are her biggest peeve.
His constant chewing is a big peeve for me.
That comment peeved the customer.
The delay peeved everyone waiting outside.

petitio.definition: a request or petition, especially in a legal or formal context
examples: They filed the petitio with the court.
The document is a petitio for review.

perennial.definition: lasting for a long time; continuing year after year
examples: The plant is perennial and comes back every spring.
This is a perennial problem in the industry.

perennial.definition: a plant that lives for more than two years and grows back each season
examples: They chose a perennial for the flower bed.
Perennials need less replanting than annuals.

patrol.definition: to move around an area to watch for danger or to make sure rules are followed
examples: Officers patrol the neighborhood at night.
They patrol the park every morning.

patrol.definition: an organized activity in which people watch or travel through an area for safety
examples: A patrol found the lost child near the river.
The patrol lasted two hours.

psyche.definition: the mind and mental processes, especially in psychology
examples: Therapy can help people understand their psyche.
Stress affected his psyche during the busy season.

ptisan.definition: a medicinal herbal drink or tea traditionally used for health
examples: Herbal ptisan was used as a gentle remedy.
The book describes how ptisan is prepared from herbs.

plop.definition: a soft, heavy sound made when something falls into water or a soft surface
examples: A plop came from the puddle as the rain hit.
I heard a plop in the sink.

plop.definition: to fall with that soft, heavy sound
examples: The book plopped onto the floor.
He plopped into the chair.

plosive.definition: describing a speech sound made by stopping airflow and then releasing it suddenly
examples: In English, p and b are plosive sounds.
The linguist studied plosive consonants.
The t is a plosive in many analyses.

presage.definition: to be a sign that something will happen in the future
examples: Dark clouds presage a storm.
Her sudden silence presaged bad news.

presage.definition: a sign or warning that suggests what will happen soon
examples: The strange smell was a presage of trouble.
He saw the decision as a presage of change.

paralogism.definition: a faulty reasoning process that leads to a wrong conclusion
examples: The debate included a paralogism that confused the issue.
She pointed out the paralogism in his argument.

pawn.definition: a chess piece with low value that moves forward and captures diagonally
examples: He moved a pawn to open the line for his bishop.
The pawn advanced two squares.

pawn.definition: a person used by others to achieve their goals
examples: He realized he had been used as a pawn.
They treated employees like pawns in the negotiation.

piecened.definition: made of pieces or in small separate parts
examples: The artwork looks piecened, like it was assembled from scraps.
Her story felt piecened rather than continuous.

pellucid.definition: very clear and easy to understand
examples: Her explanation was pellucid and well organized.
The report gives a pellucid summary of the results.

plangent.definition: loud and mournful, often used to describe sounds
examples: The plangent alarm rang throughout the building.
A plangent whistle sounded in the distance.

prow.definition: the front part of a ship
examples: The waves broke against the prow.
He stood near the prow and watched the coast.

proffer.definition: to offer something formally or politely
examples: She proffered her help after the meeting.
The company proffered a solution to the problem.

pelagic.definition: living in the open sea rather than near the shore or sea floor
examples: Pelagic fish travel far across the ocean.
They observed pelagic birds during the voyage.

pap.definition: soft, watery food or a weak, unimportant form of writing or speech
examples: The baby ate pap made from grains.
His speech was pap and did not add any useful information.

pilferer.definition: a person who steals small things, especially from places where they are kept
examples: The store caught a pilferer at the checkout.
He was known as a pilferer who took small items.

pouncer.definition: a person or thing that jumps quickly to attack, catch, or grab
examples: The dog was a pouncer during training, always moving fast.
He moved like a pouncer to catch the ball.

prop.definition: an object used in a performance to help create the scene
examples: The actor dropped the prop by accident.
The director checked every prop before filming.

prop.definition: something that supports or helps a plan, activity, or idea continue
examples: The funding was a prop for the failing company.
That policy is a prop for the economy.

prop.definition: to support something temporarily to prevent it from falling
examples: They propped the door open with a chair.
The wall was propped after the earthquake.

parsimony.definition: the habit of using too little money or giving too little, especially when it is unnecessary
examples: His parsimony prevented him from buying helpful tools.
The company showed parsimony in its spending.

plumb.definition: to measure the depth of something, especially by lowering a weight on a line
examples: They plumbed the well to see how deep it was.
The diver plumbed the water near the pier.
I can’t plumb why he reacted that way.
Scientists are trying to plumb the causes of the disease.
Hang the picture plumb on the wall.
The pole was plumb in the ground.

preface.definition: an introductory statement or short section at the beginning of a book, document, or speech
examples: The preface explains why the author wrote the book.
Read the preface before you start the chapters.

preface.definition: to introduce something with a statement that comes before it
examples: She prefaced her answer with a short apology.
The report was prefaced by a summary.

panegyrize.definition: to praise someone or something in a very enthusiastic way
examples: He panegyrized the new manager during the speech.
The article panegyrized the athlete’s achievements.

precise.definition: exact and careful; giving details that are accurate
examples: Use precise measurements when you bake.
She gave a precise explanation of the plan.

patter.definition: a continuous series of small quick sounds, often of footsteps or rain
examples: We heard a patter of rain on the roof.
The patter of footsteps in the hall kept me awake.

patter.definition: to make a series of light, repeated sounds
examples: Rain started to patter against the window.
The mice patter across the floor at night.

plateau.definition: an area of high flat land
examples: The town sits on a plateau above the valley.
A plateau covers much of the region.

placate.definition: to make someone less angry by doing or saying something reassuring
examples: The manager tried to placate the customer with an apology.
She placated him by listening first.

paralegal.definition: a person who assists a lawyer with legal work
examples: The paralegal helped organize the case files.
She works as a paralegal at a law firm.

pertinacious.definition: refusing to give up; persistent and stubborn in continuing
examples: He was pertinacious in asking follow-up questions.
Her pertinacious efforts finally paid off.

palimpsest.definition: a manuscript page where older writing was erased and new writing was added
examples: The palimpsest revealed earlier letters beneath the new ink.
Researchers studied the palimpsest to read the hidden text.
The papermaker explained how fibers become paper.
My grandfather worked as a papermaker.
